name: Omid Kordestani
current_role: Chair of the Board, Pearson plc (since 2022); non-executive director, Klarna Group
profile: Tehran-born Iranian-American executive who ran Google's worldwide sales and business operations from 1999 to 2009 (and returned as Chief Business Officer 2014-15), building the wealth tied to his early Alphabet stock. He was later executive chairman of Twitter (2015-2020) and has chaired education company Pearson since 2022.
interesting_fact: Before Google he ran OEM sales and business development at Netscape; at Google he built the global sales organisation that turned search ads into the company's revenue engine. Time named him one of its 100 people who shape our world in 2006.
deep_cut_fact: He moved to San Jose after his father died in 1976, graduated from Buchser High School in Santa Clara (1980), studied electrical engineering at San Jose State and worked as an engineer at Hewlett-Packard before his 1991 Stanford MBA.
notes: Best route is via Pearson's corporate media team (corporate/financial media contacts listed on the IR contacts page; addresses obfuscated there). Co-founded the PARSA Community Foundation for the Iranian-American community. Pearson confirmed him as chair in a Sept 2026 board announcement.

name: Rajju Shroff
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, UPL Ltd (since Dec 2022)
profile: Rajnikant 'Rajju' Shroff founded Mumbai-based UPL in 1969 to make red phosphorus and built it over 50+ years as chairman and MD into one of the world's largest crop-protection companies, especially after the $4.2bn Arysta LifeScience deal in 2018. He stepped down at 90 in Dec 2022; son Jai Shroff is now chairman and group CEO.
interesting_fact: UPL began in 1969 producing red phosphorus, which Shroff pioneered making in India. He was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2021 and Mexico's Order of the Aztec Eagle in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: A Bombay University chemistry graduate from a Kutch entrepreneurial family, in 1957 he developed a new process for making mercury salts at a UK plant, and a British company paid him royalties for it, which was rare for an Indian chemist at the time.
notes: Now about 93 and retired to focus on social causes; UPL lists upl@uniphos.com for corporate-affairs enquiries. Son Jai Shroff (chairman/CEO) is the active public face.

name: Terry Leprino
current_role: President, Leprino Foods Company Foundation; board director and co-owner, Leprino Foods (Denver)
profile: Terry Leprino and her sister Gina Vecchiarelli inherited about 90% of Denver-based Leprino Foods, the world's largest mozzarella maker (est. $3.6bn revenue; supplies Domino's, Pizza Hut, Papa John's), after their father James Leprino died in June 2025. She spent a decade as the company's marketing director, sits on its board and now leads the corporate foundation.
interesting_fact: Leprino Foods, founded by her grandfather in 1950, makes more than 1 billion pounds of cheese a year; her father pioneered the technology to make pizza cheese at industrial scale.
deep_cut_fact: She holds a bachelor's from Arizona State and a master's in biblical counseling from Colorado Christian University, where she has served as a trustee for over a decade. She also sits on the board of the Issachar Urban Leadership Center.
notes: Very private family business with no named PR contact. The media centre directs press to Corporate Communications by phone, and the contact form has a 'Media' option. The CCU trustee bio URL came up in search results but returned 404 when fetched directly.
